name: KFin Technologies Ltd
title: KFin Technologies Ltd - 543720 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: KFin Q4 FY26 revenue rose 23% YoY (4.6% ex-Ascent) as mark-to-market hits and weak Issuer Solutions held EBITDA margin to 37%; FY27 guide 23-24% revenue growth.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue grew about 23% YoY but fell 6.3% QoQ, and ex-Ascent growth was only 4.6% YoY. Mark-to-market losses on equity and metal-ETF-driven asset mix shifts, plus weaker Issuer Solutions retail folios and corporate actions, weighed on the quarter. Consolidated EBITDA margin was 37% in Q4 (ex-Ascent about 42%), and core PAT rose 3.8% YoY in the quarter and 6.2% for FY26 to INR353 crore. Management guided to conservative FY27 consolidated revenue growth of 23-24%, EBITDA growth of 16-17% (margin near 39-40%) and PAT growth of about 10%, and said it will recalibrate monthly.

financial_highlights.change: down 15.2% QoQ in EBITDA per management
EBITDA growth about 5.1% for the year
reported PAT flat after one-time Labour Code charge

segments.name: Domestic mutual fund
segments.commentary: Contributes 61% of Q4 revenue; management targets domestic MF below 50% of revenue over 5 years, currently 58% ex-3% value-added solution revenue. AUM grew in line with industry at about 21%, but revenue grew about 11% due to April 2025 pricing discounts, MTM erosion and ETF mix shift.

segments.name: Issuer Solutions
segments.commentary: Contributes 10% of Q4 revenue; both revenue and segment profit fell YoY. Management cited retail folio exodus (existing clients lost about 1.7 million folios vs 2.5-3 million added through new wins), tepid corporate actions and a base effect from a large Q4 FY25 demerger.

segments.name: AIF, private wealth and PMS
segments.commentary: Contributes 4.5% of Q4 revenue. AIF AUM grew about 19-24% and AIF fund count rose from 593 to 741, with margins above 37%; private wealth/PMS revenue fell on MTM, though 6 wealth platform wins were signed early in the year.

segments.name: Global fund services (GFS)
segments.commentary: Contributes 4.5% of Q4 revenue; management guides about 60%+ GFS growth next year, citing large RTA and fund accounting deal wins in the last three quarters, including the Philippines largest bank fund accounting contract.

segments.name: Ascent Fund Solutions (acquired October)
segments.commentary: Contributes about 15% of Q4 revenue at 8% EBITDA margin; about 499 new fund-manager clients added (about 900-950 funds). Management expects Ascent revenue growth of 25-30% and margin to move to the early teens over time.

segments.name: NPS, Reval, Hexagram
segments.commentary: Each about 1.5% of Q4 revenue. NPS AUM-linked pricing moved from per-subscriber to basis points, and pension subscribers grew about 34% vs industry 11%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue growth of about 23-24% (CFO also cited 24-25% in Q&A); management stressed this is not formal guidance.
FY27 EBITDA growth of about 16-17%, implying margin near 39%; management still aims to cross 40% and keep 40-45% over time.
FY27 PAT growth of about 10%; organic (ex-Ascent) revenue growth about 15% and PAT growth a little over 11%.
International organic revenue expected to grow over 60% and total international revenue over 70% including Ascent this year.
Of six signed Ascent $100 million-plus fund contracts, about 3.5-4 contracts' revenue assumed in FY27, up to 6 if launches are early; one started in March, three in Q1 and the rest in Q2.
Ascent yield modelled at 6-7 bps, not 10 bps; Labour Code charge will not recur from FY27.
capex_capacity: Ascent amortization of client contracts and brand (10-year life) runs about INR6 crore a quarter against PAT, expected to persist.
Synergy plan covers technology, real estate, people and shared services; cost optimisation and tighter discretionary and BD spend stated as the main levers.
Aladdin integration with mPower (fund accounting) is complex; direct integration and BD expected to start within a couple of quarters.
KRA platform went live late Q3/early Q4 FY26; over 25 AMCs and brokers signed, AMFI-chosen partner for unclaimed assets.
demand_pricing: Mutual fund AUM growth about 21% in FY26 with net flows strong; equity share hit by about 200 bps over two quarters from metal ETF growth; April early trends show ETF share reversing.

Management expects MF yield pressure to be contained: negotiated contracts for this and next year already reflect TER cuts; yield about 3 bps vs 60 bps average AMC yield, with no further TER discussions expected.
Domestic MF market share rose from 30.3% in FY22 to 32.5% in FY26; SIP market share above 37%.
Issuer Solutions expects IPO pipeline (including Jio) to revive primary issuance, with retail folios and corporate actions recovering from Q1 FY27.
Ascent yield affected by asset mix (crypto/digital currency funds); management said it is roughly 7 bps and variable by about 50 bps.

qa_highlights.question: Will domestic MF yield decline of about 4-5% YoY in FY27 still hold if metal mix stabilises?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said guidance assumes the same asset mix as end-FY26 with ETFs around 23%; it expects more active funds this year, and the 4-5% yield view was not directly reconfirmed.

qa_highlights.question: What is steady-state Issuer Solutions revenue growth after one-offs, given realisations hit harder than folios?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the decline to net folio loss (about 1.7 million existing folios lost), weak corporate actions in Q4, and a demerger base effect; it expects these to normalise from Q1 FY27 with demergers pushed from March into May.

qa_highlights.question: Why does Ascent's EBITDA-to-PAT gap widen, and is the company paying tax despite losses at Ascent?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the gap is amortisation of acquired client contracts and brand (about INR6 crore a quarter, 10-year life); operating leverage should offset it over 2-3 years. Ascent's top-line growth is 5% in USD, about 8% in INR QoQ.

qa_highlights.question: Why does FY27 EBITDA guidance imply margin below 40% after Ascent consolidation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the implied margin is about 39%, but it still aims for above 40% through cost productivity, with new-business drag and BD spend included; it expects the range to be 40-45% over time.

qa_highlights.question: Why did alternatives, private wealth and PMS revenue fall QoQ, and why is Ascent yield below its earlier 8-9 bps?
qa_highlights.answer: Private wealth/PMS fell on MTM markdowns and deferred Q3/Q4 deals; AIF AUM grew 24-25%. Ascent yield was always about 7 bps per management, moving with asset mix such as crypto funds.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for KRA revenue and Aladdin integration?
qa_highlights.answer: KRA went live late Q3/early Q4 FY26 with over 25 AMCs and brokers signed; a proposed single POS KYC ID could reduce fetch-cost revenue industry-wide. Aladdin integration is slower, with direct integration and BD expected in a couple of quarters.

risks_watch: Equity MTM volatility and market direction drive MF, AIF and PMS revenue; management says it is recalibrating guidance monthly.
Issuer Solutions depends on retail folio recovery, corporate actions and IPO timing (including Jio).
Ascent margin is 8% in Q4 and the 40% consolidated EBITDA target depends on synergy delivery and operating leverage.
Possible KRA fee pressure from a single POS KYC ID initiative.
Middle East (GCC) disruption could hit international funds, though management sees redomiciling into Singapore or Cayman as mitigant.
Q1 FY27 demerger timing and whether Ascent's six $100 million-plus contracts launch on schedule.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term growth and market share wins, but cautious on near-term numbers: management repeatedly called FY27 guidance conservative, not formal, and subject to monthly recalibration. Most candid on the drivers of the weak Q4 (MTM, retail exodus, corporate actions) and evasive on the exact FY27 margin, which it framed as roughly 39% but aiming above 40%.
key_quotes: We have assumed a fairly conservative estimate as we are moving into the coming year in terms of where we believe we will end up with high-level numbers.
we have a reasonable line of visibility to get to about 23% to 24% top line growth into the coming year.
Ascent is in the range of 6 to 7 bps and that is what you should factor if you're modeling anything.
So the precise numbers won't be able to diverge. But then it's fair to say that about 3.5 to 4 contracts worth of revenue would have been fully baked into this year

growth.why: Management guides FY27 consolidated revenue growth of about 23-24% (not formal guidance), backed partly by Ascent's six $100M+ fund contracts (3.5-4 assumed in FY27), GFS wins and 60%+ international organic growth, but no company-owned capacity additions were cited and the guide is not quantified by segment beyond these.
